description: Codex audits and retires edge functions; Claude Code verifies. Tests a rule, a path and a security explanation from the first session.

turns.user: Audit our Supabase edge functions and retire the unused ones. Rule: never delete a function outright; overwrite it with a 410 stub first so we can roll back.
turns.reply: Agreed: every retired function gets a 410 stub first, no outright deletion. I found 23 deployed functions; 7 are unused and reachable with the public anon key.
Saved exact JSON copies of all 23 functions to ~/backups/edge-2026-09-26/prod/ before touching anything.

turns.user: Check the callers of function candidate {n}.
turns.reply: Candidate {n} has no callers in the web app or the iOS app.

turns.user: Why is the anon key enough to call them?
turns.reply: Because the gateway verify_jwt check accepts the anon JWT; only an in-function auth.getUser call really requires a signed-in user.

turns.user: Continue the retirement. Which function was the riskiest?
turns.reply: fetch-url-metadata was the riskiest: it allowed server-side request forgery. It now returns 410 like the other six.
Open: delete the 12 retired functions from the dashboard, because the MCP server has no delete tool.
